To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

epithelial cell death, decidual cell penetration of the basal laminae beneath epithelial cells, and extracellular matrix modification are important steps in the process of chorioallantois formation in the rat.

epithelial cells that line the mesometrial side of the implantation chambers of rat gestation site degenerate and die, and the space between these cells and underlying decidual cells is filled by a collagenous extracellular matrix, before trophoblast cells from the conceptus invade and form the chorioallantotic placenta in that region.
trophoblastic cells do not directly cause the epithelial cells to undergo necrosis in the mesometrium of rat implantation chambers, although trophblasts may trigger or modulate these changes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the chorioallatoic placenta is not formed by a process of trophoblast invasion of the uteroplacental unit but rather by a process of epithelial cell death followed by decidual cell invasion and remodeling.

the chorioallatoic placenta is a result of the death of the uterolental epithelium, which is followed by the formation of a basal lamina and the migration and differentiation of the decidual cells into a chorionic epithelium.

trophoblastic cells do not play a direct part in the process of chorioallantois formation.
